answer: Barometric site proof: each fake costs one real device placed at its own location (~$40 plus upkeep). Every identity logs pressure each 10 minutes; verifiers compare it with weather stations within 20 km. A device claiming a shale ridge at 900 m must read about 90 hPa below the valley, and when a gale front passes, real sensors show the drop at times matching their positions. Racks of phones in one room give identical curves and are merged into one identity, so the "many cities" fable fails at the first storm. Traces can't be shared or bulk-bought: one sensor, one place.
